"""Polynomial-time reduction from SAT (CNF satisfiability) to Clique.

Standard Karp reduction:
  * One vertex per literal occurrence in the formula.
  * Two vertices are joined by an edge iff they come from different clauses
    and their literals are not contradictory (i.e. not v and -v).
  * k = number of clauses.

within a clause), and the pairwise non-contradiction guarantees a single
consistent truth assignment can set all chosen literals true.  Conversely,
a satisfying assignment yields such a clique by choosing one true literal
per clause.

Edge cases:
  * No clauses -> k = 0, and a clique of size >= 0 always exists; SAT with
    no clauses is yes.  Consistent.
  * An empty clause contributes no vertex, so no clique can reach k when at
    least one clause exists; SAT with an empty clause is no.  Consistent.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map a SAT instance to a Clique instance with the same yes/no answer."""
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    # Give every literal occurrence a vertex, remembering its clause and sign.
    vertex_clause = []   # vertex -> index of its clause
    vertex_lit = []      # vertex -> the literal (nonzero int)
    for ci, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for lit in clause:
            vertex_clause.append(ci)
            vertex_lit.append(lit)

    n = len(vertex_lit)

    edges = []
    for i in range(n):
        ci = vertex_clause[i]
        li = vertex_lit[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            # No edge between two literals of the same clause.
            if vertex_clause[j] == ci:
                continue
            # No edge between contradictory literals (v and -v).
            if li == -vertex_lit[j]:
                continue
            edges.append([i, j])

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": len(clauses)}
